title: Equality in the flow-value/cut-capacity bound
statement: Let $N$ be a network with capacity function $c$, distinguished source $x$ and sink $y$, let $f$ be a flow in $N$, and let $S$ be a vertex set defining a cut, so that $x \in S$ and $y \notin S$; write $\bar S$ for the complementary vertex set. Then the value of the flow equals the capacity of the cut, $\mathrm{val}(f) = \mathrm{cap}(S,\bar S)$, if and only if $f(u,v) = c(u,v)$ for every arc with $u \in S$ and $v \in \bar S$ (each forward arc across the cut is saturated) and $f(u,v) = 0$ for every arc with $u \in \bar S$ and $v \in S$ (each backward arc across the cut carries no flow).
hypotheses_covered: N is a network (disjoint nonempty source and sink sets, capacity function)
f is a flow in N (capacity constraint and conservation at intermediate vertices)
S defines a cut: x ∈ S and y ∉ S
